minutes.headline: Select Board adopted tri-board ground rules to launch the FY27 school/town budget process, plus several appointments.
minutes.summary: The Select Board handled a full agenda of appointments (Adam Bernie to planning board, Cara McCarthy as communications/IT manager, Tiffany Warren to Cultural Council), heard a town manager report covering a state supplemental school funding award, Wallace Park damage, and staffing vacancies, and reviewed ARPA project balances nearing their spending deadline. Much of the meeting was devoted to setting FY2026 town manager and select board goals and adopting ground rules for a new joint "tri-board" process with the school committee and finance committee aimed at producing a select board recommendation on the FY27 budget, including possible cuts, level funding, or a Prop 2½ override, by around February 2026. The board closed by entering executive session for town manager contract negotiations and police union bargaining strategy.

what_happened.line: The Select Board adopted ground rules for a joint select board/school committee/finance committee "tri-board" process on the FY27 budget.
The board set a target of a tri-board budget recommendation by February 2026, covering cuts, level funding, or a Prop 2½ override.
The board approved revised FY2026 town manager goals and FY26 select board goals.
The board appointed Adam Bernie to the planning board, ratified Cara McCarthy as communications/IT manager, and appointed Tiffany Warren to the Cultural Council.
The town manager reviewed ARPA project balances nearing their spending deadline, including an unexplained remainder on a dump truck purchase to be researched.

why_it_matters: The tri-board process is the mechanism that will produce a recommendation to residents on the FY27 school and town budget, including whether a Proposition 2½ override goes to a vote.
Tri-board meetings will not hold their own public comment period, though residents can still raise budget concerns at each board's regular meetings.
Unspent ARPA funds nearing their deadline touch a parks project, fire department equipment, and a municipal building project, and any unresolved remainder risks being lost.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every substantive vote we captured, all unanimous, and on most of the ARPA and budget figures, apart from caption misspellings of names and one figure ($3,57,970.58). The key difference is that the official minutes record a vote our minutes lack (approval of the December 3 and 10, 2024 minutes, 4-0-1 with one abstention) and none of the tri-board scheduling, location and public-comment decisions we recorded.
